title: The Set Monster
author: Isaac Banner
notes: The Caller's Box 18307, permission: full. A becket dance with a **triple progression**: every dancer moves three dancing places, which is `progression: { lark: 3, robin: 3 }` and goes through `progressSet`'s uniform path with nothing else changed - no refusal, no special case. What the dance reaches for is the other end of the set: N2 in A2, N3 in B1 and N4 twice, in B1 and B2. **Still owed, and it is three faults rather than one** (M9c; M8b's becket `N_k` table is settled and the relations resolve now). Closure passes at 0.0000 px at every checked length. (1) **`collision`** fails at all eight. At six couples the worst is **0.863 px at beat 67.625**, inside A1's `balance-ring` of the second time through: the triple progression maps two whole hands-fours on to each other's places, and the first gatherer of the next time through walks `c1/lark` from (-16, 40) to (-16, 80) while `c3/robin` walks the same line from (-16, 100) to (-16, 60). At four couples it is 0.000 px at beat 64, where B2's two partner swings settle four dancers on **two** floor points - the same shared-pool fault Contrablend has - and the two wait groups then faithfully copy it. (2) **`reach`** fails at 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 12, and it is four figures rather than one: `long-lines` (11.2162-63.6705 px), `pull-by` (5.73-20.68), the partner `swing` (5.48-33.26) and `balance-ring` (up to 12.82). The cause is upstream of all of them - A2's `pull-by` with `pairs: "N2"` is a **66.5 px pull-by danced in two beats** at twelve couples, because in becket N2 really is two couple places away, and everything downstream inherits the scatter: B1's long line has members up to 86 px off the line, holding hands. **The direction is the opposite of what M9b expected**: at four couples, where N2, N3 and N4 all name nobody and half the dance is hold-place, reach all but passes (1.1737 px in `robins-chain`), and at six it passes outright. The failures appear exactly where N2 *does* name somebody. **Two readings recorded rather than measured.** B1's "(4) In long lines, go forward (facing out)" is written as a four-beat `long-lines`, which goes forward and back in four rather than forward only, because the figure has no parameter for half of itself or for which way the line faces. The interrupted square through's `(N3R;PL)` is written as its two pairings out of the N3 ring's own four stations, so that "N3 by the right" is the pair across the ring and "partner by the left" is the pair beside each other. **FR-C1: `N2` is one couple place, not two (E3, DD49), and this dance moved.** Becket's `N_k` is now the k-th couple along the set the way your own couple progresses, one couple place a step, so A2's `pull-by` with `pairs: "N2"`, B1's N3 and B1/B2's N4 all reach half as far as they did. The sentence above - "a 66.5 px pull-by danced in two beats at twelve couples, because in becket N2 really is two couple places away" - is **withdrawn**: N2 is one couple place away. Measured on M10's planted gait, before -> after, at every checked length, reach worst short: 4c 1.9221 -> 1.9221, 5c 11.2162 -> **6.5390**, 6c **pass -> 6.5390 FAIL**, 7c 24.6401 -> 27.1250, 8c 25.9602 -> **22.1892**, 9c 40.7595 -> **19.8332**, 10c 27.5183 -> **21.0889**, 12c 63.6705 -> **26.2415**. Collision: 4c 1.851 unchanged, 5c 0.019 -> **1.556**, 6c 0.863 unchanged, 7c 0.019 unchanged, 8c 0.056 -> 0.019, 9c/10c/12c 0.000 unchanged. Closure stays 0.0000 px everywhere and `progressed` is **40.0000 px at every length from five up** where it used to read 68.0000/51.2250/40.0000 by parity. So the change is a large net improvement in reach - the long line at twelve couples is 26 px out of reach rather than 64 - and **one honest regression: six couples used to pass reach and now fails it at 6.5390 px**. The dance fails collision at all eight lengths either way and is not promoted. The per-figure split in the paragraph above (`long-lines` 11.2162-63.6705, `pull-by` 5.73-20.68, the partner `swing` 5.48-33.26, `balance-ring` up to 12.82) was measured against the old table and has **not** been re-derived; the per-length worsts here have. **FR-C2: the half-width slide, and what a triple progression means in it.** A becket line slides half a couple width a time through (DD54), so the two lines pass each other one couple place per progression and `{"lark": 3, "robin": 3}` is three of those - the card's own triple progression, three couple places of relative travel, which is the couple you meet being three along. No conversion is written anywhere: `progressSet` applies the formation's own `Progression.next` once per place, and one place now is one couple place of *meeting* even though it is half a couple place of *travel*. `becketMeeting.test.ts` measures what that does to a hall - every length in its table mixes completely except **six couples**, where a triple progression closes on part of the ring and each couple meets only one or two of the other five. Measured before -> after at every checked length: closure 0.0000 px unchanged; `progressed` 51.2250 at four couples and 40.0000 at five and up -> a uniform **20.0000**; reach worst short 1.9221/6.5390/6.5390/27.1250/22.1892/19.8332/21.0889/26.2415 -> 1.9221/10.9326/14.3567/14.3567/19.8332/21.0889/26.2415/26.2415 at 4-12; collision 1.851/1.556/0.863/0.019/0.019/0.000/0.000/0.000 -> 1.050/0.056/0.246/0.056/0.728/0.056/0.513/0.210. **Not promoted, and the one measured thing is collision**, 0.056-1.050 px at every length: B2's two partner swings settle four dancers on two floor points (Contrablend's shared-pool fault, M9d/M9e's known gap), which FR-C2 does not touch. `progressed` is the second: nothing in the record carries the slide. **M9g: the shared point is not a pool and not the ledger, and the number underneath it is `progressed`.** Measured at five couples, beat 74.875: the two instances of A1's neighbour `swing` in group `p1.5` share one floor point because `anchor: "meet"` puts each pair at the midpoint of its own two **bodies**, and after the boundary the two pairs are the two **diagonals** of one rectangle - `1L-2R` is `c1/robin (-16, 100)` with `c3/lark (16, 80)` and `1R-2L` is `c1/lark (16, 100)` with `c3/robin (-16, 80)` - whose midpoints are both `(0, 90)`. A meeting point is not a place, so it is never in a pool and M9d's claims ledger cannot see it; FR-C2's attribution of this number to "B2's two partner swings" is **withdrawn** - it is A1's neighbour swing of the time through after the boundary. Why the pairs are diagonal is the whole of it: **every one of the ten dancers is exactly 20.0000 px from the seat the progression gives them at beat 64**, line 0 wanting -20 along the set and line 1 +20, which is one becket half-shift (DD54) and is what `progressed 20.0000` has been saying at every length since FR-C2. Nothing in this record slides: Butter is the same dance shape with `slide-left` written into its card and reads `progressed 0.0000`. Are You 'Most Done? is the proof of what closes it (M9g item 1): the moment a figure carried its progression, its closure, reach and collision all went green together. This dance has no such figure and the card gives it none, so **nothing was invented here**; `startPlaces` would read 0 and move none of the geometry, which is oracle-tuning. Not promoted, and the one measured thing is now `progressed 20.0000 px` - one becket half-shift, at every checked length, carried by nothing.
